## Neighboring Countries

Singapore’s territory consists of one main island and 63 satellite islands. This means that **the country doesn’t share land borders with any other countries**. The closest countries to Singapore are Malaysia and Singapore.

## Maritime Borders of Singapore

[![Image 5: Map of Singapore and surrounding waters.](https://www.mappr.co/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/singapore-map-576x432.jpg)](https://cdn.mappr.co/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/singapore-map.jpg)
Singapore borders four different bodies of water: the Strait of Malacca to the west, the Singapore Strait to the south, the South China Sea to the east, and the Straits of Johor to the north.

## Administrative Divisions of Singapore

[![Image 6: A vector map of Singapore and its five districts.](https://www.mappr.co/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/Singapore-district-map-450x450.jpg)](https://cdn.mappr.co/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/Singapore-district-map.jpg)

The five Community Development Council Districts of Singapore

Singapore is a city-state, which means that the entire country is coterminous with the city of Singapore. As such, there are no large-scale divisions such as provinces or states. Instead, Singapore is divided into Community Development Council Districts (CDCs), town councils, and electoral constituencies.

There are currently [five CDCs in Singapore](https://www.cdc.gov.sg/who-we-are/five-districts/), each of which is managed by a Council that is headed by a mayor. CDCs are responsible for managing community programs to promote community bonding and social cohesion.

Each CDC is further divided into town councils, [of which there are 17](https://www.mnd.gov.sg/our-work/regulating-town-councils/about-town-councils). Town councils manage the day-to-day operations of residential and commercial property within the town. The smallest administrative division in Singapore is the electoral constituency. There are [31 constituencies in Singapore](https://www.parliament.gov.sg/mps/find-mps-in-my-constituency).

There are also five [regions of Singapore](https://www.mappr.co/counties/regions-of-singapore/) that remain constant and are not used for statistical electoral purposes.

## Geography of Singapore

![Image 7: A small body of water at Dairy Farm Nature Park in Singapore](https://www.mappr.co/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/dairy-farm-park-singapore-576x324.jpg)

Dairy Farm Nature Park

Located just off the southern end of the Malay Peninsula, Singapore consists of its main island of Pulau Ujong in addition to 63 smaller islands. Singapore is separated from Malaysia by the Johor Straits, though the two are connected via the Johor-Singapore Causeway and the Tuas Second Link.

Singapore has a [total land area of 734.3 km2](https://www.singstat.gov.sg/find-data/search-by-theme/society/environment/latest-data) (283.5 sq mi), which makes it the 20 th smallest country in the world. Most of this land area has been urbanized, and 100% of the country’s population lives in an urban area.

There are four [nature reserves in Singapore](https://www.nparks.gov.sg/biodiversity/our-ecosystems/nature-areas-and-nature-reserves) as well as 20 additional nature areas. Singapore has lost around 95% of its historical forests, but efforts are being made to make the city greener and to preserve the remaining wildlife.

## History of Singapore

Recorded history in Singapore dates to well over a thousand years ago and was part of both the Srivijaya and Majapahit empires. Although the veracity of records in the Malay Annals is often the subject of debate, they claim that the Kingdom of Singapura was founded in 1299.

By the 14 th century, Singapore’s main island functioned as a trading port known as Temasek. After Parameswara, the last king of Singapura, was driven out at the end of the 14 th century, the main settlement was likely abandoned.

The colonial era in Singapore began with the arrival of British governor Stamford Raffles in 1819. He signed a [Treaty of Friendship and Alliance](https://www.roots.gov.sg/en/stories-landing/stories/the-singapore-story-through-60-objects/colonial/treaty-of-friendship-and-alliance/story) along with Sultan Hussein and the Temenggong Abdul Rahman the same year which allowed the British to set up a trading post that would be jointly administered by the British and Malay rulers. This is officially recognized as the founding of Singapore.

Singapore went on to become an important trading center and a global center for rubber export. It became a British crown colony in 1867.

During World War II, Singapore was invaded by the Japanese during the [Battle of Singapore](http://news.bbc.co.uk/onthisday/hi/dates/stories/february/15/newsid_3529000/3529447.stm) and was subsequently occupied by Japan until the end of the war in 1945. The period of occupation was marked by hardships suffered by local people and the death of thousands during the Sook Ching Massacre.

In the years that followed the second world war, Singapore moved towards self-governance and independence. After briefly merging with Malaysia, Singapore became fully independent in 1965.

Since independence, Singapore’s economy has continued to strengthen and grow, and the People’s Action Party (PAP) has remained in power.

## Culture and People of Singapore

### People

![Image 8: People walk across a colorful intersection in Singapore's Little India district. ](https://www.mappr.co/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/singapore-march-5-little-india-district-576x384.jpg)

Little India district, Singapore

The total [population of Singapore](https://www.singstat.gov.sg/find-data/search-by-theme/population/population-and-population-structure/latest-data) as of 2022 is 5,637,000. Lower fertility rates and longer life expectancies are leading to an aging population in the country, something that has been [a struggle for the country](https://www.reuters.com/article/uk-singapore-babies/tiny-singapore-risks-economic-gloom-without-big-baby-boom-idUKLNE87U00H20120831) for more than a decade.

The largest ethnic groups in Singapore are of Chinese, Malay, and Indian descent, of which the Chinese population is the largest. These ethnicities and the country’s colonial past are represented in the country’s four official languages: Mandarin Chinese, Malay, Tamil, and English. Racial and religious harmony is considered a cornerstone of Singapore’s success.

### Cuisine

![Image 9: A table full of many local food dishes in Singapore. ](https://www.mappr.co/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/local-singapore-food-576x384.jpg)

Local Singaporean food

Singaporean cuisine is notable for its variety. It’s easy to find Chinese, Malay, and Indian food in Singapore, along with fusion foods. Peranakan cuisine, for example, is a mix of Chinese and Malay cuisines that originated in Singapore.

The national dish of Singapore is considered Hainanese chicken rice, which is based on Wenchang chicken, a Hainanese dish.

### Art

![Image 10: Musicians perform on a stage at Marina Bay in Singapore. ](https://www.mappr.co/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/singapore-november-12-2016-young-modern-576x384.jpg)

Music performance at Marina Bay, Singapore

There is a variety of art museums in Singapore, including the National Gallery Singapore, the Singapore Art Museum, and the ArtScience Museum, among others. The blend of ethnicities and cultures in Singapore can be seen in the literature produced in the country, sometimes referred to as “[SingLit](https://singlit.world/),” and in the various musical styles performed at festivals.

## Government and Politics in Singapore

The government of Singapore is a parliamentary republic, and the supreme law of the country comes from the [Constitution of Singapore](https://sso.agc.gov.sg/Act/CONS1963). The President is the head of state, and the Prime Minister is the head of the government.

The President of Singapore is elected by popular vote, and Halima Yacob, the country’s first female president, was [elected in 2017](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2017/9/13/halimah-yacob-named-singapores-first-female-president). The Prime Minister is appointed by the President from among the Members of Parliament.

## Tourist Attractions of Singapore

As a major [aviation hub in Asia](https://www.travelandleisure.com/singapore-changi-airport-major-southeast-asia-aviation-hub-6751382), millions of passengers pass through Singapore every year. But there are many [exciting things to do in Singapore](https://www.getyourguide.com/singapore-l169042/?partner_id=HDHQ696&utm_medium=online_publisher&cmp=singapore) as well. Read on to learn about some of the top tourist attractions in the country.

### China Town

![Image 11: A backdrop of skyscrapers can be seen behind the Buddha Tooth Relic Temple in Singapore's Chinatown. ](https://www.mappr.co/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/china-town-singapore-march-16-2015-576x384.jpg)

Buddha Tooth Relic Temple in Singapore’s Chinatown

For eclectic souvenirs, authentic Chinese food, and great shopping options, Singapore’s Chinatown is hard to beat. In addition to food and shopping, there are significant landmarks like the Chinatown Heritage Center, Thian Hock Keng Temple, and [Buddha Tooth Relic Temple](https://www.buddhatoothrelictemple.org.sg/).

### Singapore Botanic Gardens

![Image 12: A sculpture of swans in flights is on display at Swan Lake in the Singapore Botanic Gardens. ](https://www.mappr.co/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/singapore-16-oct-2021-flight-swans-576x324.jpg)

Swan Lake at the Singapore Botanic Gardens

The Singapore Botanic Gardens, established in 1859, has been a [UNESCO World Heritage Site](https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1483/) since 2015. It’s home to over 1,000 species of orchid in the National Orchid Garden and is [free to visit](https://www.nparks.gov.sg/sbg/visit-us).

### Marina Bay Sands

![Image 13: The Marina Bay Sands Hotel in Singapore can be seen towering over the water.](https://www.mappr.co/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/singaporefeb-7-2015-marina-bay-sands-576x384.jpg)

Marina Bay Sands Hotel in Singapore

This is likely the most iconic building in Singapore. A futuristic design makes the building stand out, and it features a casino, hotel, science museum, and convention center, among other things. It’s a focal point of Marina Bay and nearly impossible to miss.

## Transportation and Infrastructure of Singapore

The most common way for travelers to arrive in Singapore is via a flight to Changi Airport, which is one of the [busiest airports in the world](https://www.thestar.com.my/aseanplus/aseanplus-news/2023/04/09/singapore039s-changi-ranks-ninth-among-worlds-busiest-airports-in-2022-for-international-passengers#:~:text=The%20airport%20was%20the%20world's,ACI)%20World%20released%20last%20Wednesday.).

Fortunately for visitors, navigating Singapore is made easy with the country’s Mass Rapid Transit (MRT) and bus system networks. This is especially true for visiting popular attractions, most of which are near MRT stations.

There are a variety of [transportation passes for tourists](https://thesingaporetouristpass.com.sg/type-of-passes/) that offer unlimited rides on public transportation for one to three days.

## Climate and Weather of Singapore

Singapore is located [near the equator](https://www.mappr.co/thematic-maps/equator-map/) and experiences high temperatures all year. It has a tropical rainforest climate with abundant rainfall and high humidity that doesn’t show great month-to-month variation.

There are [two monsoon seasons in Singapore](http://www.weather.gov.sg/climate-climate-of-singapore/), the Northeast Monsoon and the Southeast Monsoon, which are separated by inter-monsoonal periods.

# Where is Singapore?

Singapore has a well-earned reputation as a multicultural nation with strict laws and a powerful economy, but not everyone can point to it on a map. So where is Singapore?

**Singapore is located in Southeast Asia and is part of the Asian continent.**

## Precise Location Coordinates of Singapore

[![Image 3: A red pin shows the location of Singapore on the world map.](https://www.mappr.co/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/red-pin-on-singapore-world-map-576x384.jpg)](https://cdn.mappr.co/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/red-pin-on-singapore-world-map.jpg)
The DMS (Degrees, Minutes, Seconds) coordinates for the center of Singapore are:

*   **1° 21′ 7.50” N**
*   **103° 49′ 11.41” E**

The latitude and longitude of Singapore are:

*   **Latitude:**1.352083
*   **Longitude:**103.819836

### Singapore Interesting Facts

![Image 4: The Merlion sculpture shoots water into the bay at Merlion Park in Singapore. ](https://www.mappr.co/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/singapore-january-1-2016-night-view-576x384.jpg)

Merlion Park, Singapore

## Neighboring Countries

Singapore’s territory consists of one main island and 63 satellite islands. This means that **the country doesn’t share land borders with any other countries**. The closest countries to Singapore are Malaysia and Singapore.

## Maritime Borders of Singapore

[![Image 5: Map of Singapore and surrounding waters.](https://www.mappr.co/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/singapore-map-576x432.jpg)](https://cdn.mappr.co/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/singapore-map.jpg)
Singapore borders four different bodies of water: the Strait of Malacca to the west, the Singapore Strait to the south, the South China Sea to the east, and the Straits of Johor to the north.

## Administrative Divisions of Singapore

[![Image 6: A vector map of Singapore and its five districts.](https://www.mappr.co/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/Singapore-district-map-450x450.jpg)](https://cdn.mappr.co/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/Singapore-district-map.jpg)

The five Community Development Council Districts of Singapore

Singapore is a city-state, which means that the entire country is coterminous with the city of Singapore. As such, there are no large-scale divisions such as provinces or states. Instead, Singapore is divided into Community Development Council Districts (CDCs), town councils, and electoral constituencies.

There are currently [five CDCs in Singapore](https://www.cdc.gov.sg/who-we-are/five-districts/), each of which is managed by a Council that is headed by a mayor. CDCs are responsible for managing community programs to promote community bonding and social cohesion.

Each CDC is further divided into town councils, [of which there are 17](https://www.mnd.gov.sg/our-work/regulating-town-councils/about-town-councils). Town councils manage the day-to-day operations of residential and commercial property within the town. The smallest administrative division in Singapore is the electoral constituency. There are [31 constituencies in Singapore](https://www.parliament.gov.sg/mps/find-mps-in-my-constituency).

There are also five [regions of Singapore](https://www.mappr.co/counties/regions-of-singapore/) that remain constant and are not used for statistical electoral purposes.

![Image 7: A small body of water at Dairy Farm Nature Park in Singapore](https://www.mappr.co/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/dairy-farm-park-singapore-576x324.jpg)

Dairy Farm Nature Park

Located just off the southern end of the Malay Peninsula, Singapore consists of its main island of Pulau Ujong in addition to 63 smaller islands. Singapore is separated from Malaysia by the Johor Straits, though the two are connected via the Johor-Singapore Causeway and the Tuas Second Link.

Singapore has a [total land area of 734.3 km2](https://www.singstat.gov.sg/find-data/search-by-theme/society/environment/latest-data) (283.5 sq mi), which makes it the 20 th smallest country in the world. Most of this land area has been urbanized, and 100% of the country’s population lives in an urban area.

There are four [nature reserves in Singapore](https://www.nparks.gov.sg/biodiversity/our-ecosystems/nature-areas-and-nature-reserves) as well as 20 additional nature areas. Singapore has lost around 95% of its historical forests, but efforts are being made to make the city greener and to preserve the remaining wildlife.

## History of Singapore

Recorded history in Singapore dates to well over a thousand years ago and was part of both the Srivijaya and Majapahit empires. Although the veracity of records in the Malay Annals is often the subject of debate, they claim that the Kingdom of Singapura was founded in 1299.

By the 14 th century, Singapore’s main island functioned as a trading port known as Temasek. After Parameswara, the last king of Singapura, was driven out at the end of the 14 th century, the main settlement was likely abandoned.

The colonial era in Singapore began with the arrival of British governor Stamford Raffles in 1819. He signed a [Treaty of Friendship and Alliance](https://www.roots.gov.sg/en/stories-landing/stories/the-singapore-story-through-60-objects/colonial/treaty-of-friendship-and-alliance/story) along with Sultan Hussein and the Temenggong Abdul Rahman the same year which allowed the British to set up a trading post that would be jointly administered by the British and Malay rulers. This is officially recognized as the founding of Singapore.

Singapore went on to become an important trading center and a global center for rubber export. It became a British crown colony in 1867.

During World War II, Singapore was invaded by the Japanese during the [Battle of Singapore](http://news.bbc.co.uk/onthisday/hi/dates/stories/february/15/newsid_3529000/3529447.stm) and was subsequently occupied by Japan until the end of the war in 1945. The period of occupation was marked by hardships suffered by local people and the death of thousands during the Sook Ching Massacre.

In the years that followed the second world war, Singapore moved towards self-governance and independence. After briefly merging with Malaysia, Singapore became fully independent in 1965.

Since independence, Singapore’s economy has continued to strengthen and grow, and the People’s Action Party (PAP) has remained in power.

## Culture and People of Singapore

### People

![Image 8: People walk across a colorful intersection in Singapore's Little India district. ](https://www.mappr.co/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/singapore-march-5-little-india-district-576x384.jpg)

Little India district, Singapore

The total [population of Singapore](https://www.singstat.gov.sg/find-data/search-by-theme/population/population-and-population-structure/latest-data) as of 2022 is 5,637,000. Lower fertility rates and longer life expectancies are leading to an aging population in the country, something that has been [a struggle for the country](https://www.reuters.com/article/uk-singapore-babies/tiny-singapore-risks-economic-gloom-without-big-baby-boom-idUKLNE87U00H20120831) for more than a decade.

The largest ethnic groups in Singapore are of Chinese, Malay, and Indian descent, of which the Chinese population is the largest. These ethnicities and the country’s colonial past are represented in the country’s four official languages: Mandarin Chinese, Malay, Tamil, and English. Racial and religious harmony is considered a cornerstone of Singapore’s success.

### Cuisine

![Image 9: A table full of many local food dishes in Singapore. ](https://www.mappr.co/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/local-singapore-food-576x384.jpg)

Local Singaporean food

Singaporean cuisine is notable for its variety. It’s easy to find Chinese, Malay, and Indian food in Singapore, along with fusion foods. Peranakan cuisine, for example, is a mix of Chinese and Malay cuisines that originated in Singapore.

The national dish of Singapore is considered Hainanese chicken rice, which is based on Wenchang chicken, a Hainanese dish.

### Art

![Image 10: Musicians perform on a stage at Marina Bay in Singapore. ](https://www.mappr.co/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/singapore-november-12-2016-young-modern-576x384.jpg)

Music performance at Marina Bay, Singapore

There is a variety of art museums in Singapore, including the National Gallery Singapore, the Singapore Art Museum, and the ArtScience Museum, among others. The blend of ethnicities and cultures in Singapore can be seen in the literature produced in the country, sometimes referred to as “[SingLit](https://singlit.world/),” and in the various musical styles performed at festivals.

## Government and Politics in Singapore

The government of Singapore is a parliamentary republic, and the supreme law of the country comes from the [Constitution of Singapore](https://sso.agc.gov.sg/Act/CONS1963). The President is the head of state, and the Prime Minister is the head of the government.

The President of Singapore is elected by popular vote, and Halima Yacob, the country’s first female president, was [elected in 2017](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2017/9/13/halimah-yacob-named-singapores-first-female-president). The Prime Minister is appointed by the President from among the Members of Parliament.

## Tourist Attractions of Singapore

As a major [aviation hub in Asia](https://www.travelandleisure.com/singapore-changi-airport-major-southeast-asia-aviation-hub-6751382), millions of passengers pass through Singapore every year. But there are many [exciting things to do in Singapore](https://www.getyourguide.com/singapore-l169042/?partner_id=HDHQ696&utm_medium=online_publisher&cmp=singapore) as well. Read on to learn about some of the top tourist attractions in the country.

### China Town

![Image 11: A backdrop of skyscrapers can be seen behind the Buddha Tooth Relic Temple in Singapore's Chinatown. ](https://www.mappr.co/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/china-town-singapore-march-16-2015-576x384.jpg)

Buddha Tooth Relic Temple in Singapore’s Chinatown

For eclectic souvenirs, authentic Chinese food, and great shopping options, Singapore’s Chinatown is hard to beat. In addition to food and shopping, there are significant landmarks like the Chinatown Heritage Center, Thian Hock Keng Temple, and [Buddha Tooth Relic Temple](https://www.buddhatoothrelictemple.org.sg/).

### Singapore Botanic Gardens

![Image 12: A sculpture of swans in flights is on display at Swan Lake in the Singapore Botanic Gardens. ](https://www.mappr.co/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/singapore-16-oct-2021-flight-swans-576x324.jpg)

Swan Lake at the Singapore Botanic Gardens

The Singapore Botanic Gardens, established in 1859, has been a [UNESCO World Heritage Site](https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1483/) since 2015. It’s home to over 1,000 species of orchid in the National Orchid Garden and is [free to visit](https://www.nparks.gov.sg/sbg/visit-us).

### Marina Bay Sands

![Image 13: The Marina Bay Sands Hotel in Singapore can be seen towering over the water.](https://www.mappr.co/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/singaporefeb-7-2015-marina-bay-sands-576x384.jpg)

Marina Bay Sands Hotel in Singapore

This is likely the most iconic building in Singapore. A futuristic design makes the building stand out, and it features a casino, hotel, science museum, and convention center, among other things. It’s a focal point of Marina Bay and nearly impossible to miss.

## Transportation and Infrastructure of Singapore

The most common way for travelers to arrive in Singapore is via a flight to Changi Airport, which is one of the [busiest airports in the world](https://www.thestar.com.my/aseanplus/aseanplus-news/2023/04/09/singapore039s-changi-ranks-ninth-among-worlds-busiest-airports-in-2022-for-international-passengers#:~:text=The%20airport%20was%20the%20world's,ACI)%20World%20released%20last%20Wednesday.).

Fortunately for visitors, navigating Singapore is made easy with the country’s Mass Rapid Transit (MRT) and bus system networks. This is especially true for visiting popular attractions, most of which are near MRT stations.

There are a variety of [transportation passes for tourists](https://thesingaporetouristpass.com.sg/type-of-passes/) that offer unlimited rides on public transportation for one to three days.

## Climate and Weather of Singapore

Singapore is located [near the equator](https://www.mappr.co/thematic-maps/equator-map/) and experiences high temperatures all year. It has a tropical rainforest climate with abundant rainfall and high humidity that doesn’t show great month-to-month variation.

There are [two monsoon seasons in Singapore](http://www.weather.gov.sg/climate-climate-of-singapore/), the Northeast Monsoon and the Southeast Monsoon, which are separated by inter-monsoonal periods.

# Top 4 Football Academies in Spain Which one to choose?

You want to join a football academy, you have read a lot about it, you have asked in forums, in social networks and you are still not sure how to do it and which one to choose to become a professional player.

I hear you. Many of us have gone through this. In this article I will explain what you should take into account before, during and after recruitment.

Below you will find a table with the results of the best academy and we will tell you in detail why. This way you will have everything clearer and you will get it right the first time.

## Comparative guide to the best International Football Academies in Spain

 [raptabla id=’29146′] 
## **Before you decide, you should try a short-term programme.**

Many high performance schools and most professional football academies in general will always give you the option to try before you sign up for an annual programme.

This is because they should be able to assess you, both athletically and psychologically, to ensure that you can successfully complete the programme. As well as clarifying the educational options and homologation of studies.

This programme should include a thorough health check and serve to clarify your goals and how they can help you achieve them, while experiencing part of the programme you will have during the academic year.

## **Under 3 months programme**

Below you will find the offers of the different programmes in order to take into account their differences.

 [raptabla id=’29302′] 
The Short-Term Programme is a course of assessment, personalised coaching and advanced methodology whose main objective is to evaluate both the strengths and weaknesses of a player, as well as the opportunities and threats he will encounter on his path to elite football.

This is the best way to get a taste of what the annual programme is like for the football academy players. It includes everything in the annual programme except the educational offer and options.

The course, which lasts between one and four weeks, can also be used to assess the student’s possible entry into the Professional Programme. In the case of Kaptiva it is only offered for one week. Soccer Inter-Action, however, allows for 1 week to 3 months, making it the most flexible of the three.

## Choosing the right football academy without getting it wrong (detailed guide)

By following this checklist you won’t go wrong and you will be able to really see where the difference is.

### **Aspects to take into account when hiring a football academy**

The following annual programmes of football academies in Spain that we are going to show you on this page meet the following requirements (which would be desirable in a quality professional academy)

### **FACILITIES**

*   Ask if they are owned or rented. If they have all types of surfaces to train on. The availability of natural grass pitches is only available at professional facilities such as the SIA Academy and professional clubs.
*   Is there a beach nearby to practice on sand?

![Image 15: IMG Academy](https://soccerinteraction.com/wp-content/plugins/a3-lazy-load/assets/images/lazy_placeholder.gif)

![Image 17: barcelona en sia academy](https://soccerinteraction.com/wp-content/plugins/a3-lazy-load/assets/images/lazy_placeholder.gif)

![Image 19: Fundacion Marcet](https://soccerinteraction.com/wp-content/plugins/a3-lazy-load/assets/images/lazy_placeholder.gif)
*   If the rooms are double or single rooms or shared rooms, is there an extra charge for the double room offer?
*   It has a swimming pool and leisure rooms.

![Image 21: piscina sia academy](https://soccerinteraction.com/wp-content/plugins/a3-lazy-load/assets/images/lazy_placeholder.gif)
*   Do you have gymnasiums and fitness rooms on site?

![Image 23: salas de fitness](https://soccerinteraction.com/wp-content/plugins/a3-lazy-load/assets/images/lazy_placeholder.gif)

![Image 25: Instalaciones Kaptiva](https://soccerinteraction.com/wp-content/plugins/a3-lazy-load/assets/images/lazy_placeholder.gif)

![Image 27: aula video analisis](https://soccerinteraction.com/wp-content/plugins/a3-lazy-load/assets/images/lazy_placeholder.gif)
*   Is the type of menu in the restaurant adapted to players or is it buffet style? Is there a menu for vegans or vegetarians. Halal. Cooking workshop etc. ….

![Image 29: cafeteria soccer inter action](https://soccerinteraction.com/wp-content/plugins/a3-lazy-load/assets/images/lazy_placeholder.gif)

![Image 31: clinicanmédica](https://soccerinteraction.com/wp-content/plugins/a3-lazy-load/assets/images/lazy_placeholder.gif)

*   Analysts and scouting staff.

Are they the academy’s **own teams** trained with the methodology and coaches on staff, or do they offer you to join other collaborating clubs that do not guarantee your development or the knowledge of everything you do during the week?

The academy has a multidisciplinary team, consisting of the coaching staff, nutritionist, physical trainer, sports doctor and psychologist.

#### **PHYSICAL PREPARATION AND INJURY RECOVERY**

The physical preparation department of a football academy is responsible for optimising the performance of the players and minimising the risk of injury.

## What types of football academies are there and which one to choose according to your needs?

There are the following types of academies according to our criteria, which we summarise below;

### **Club youth academies**

Most clubs recognise that the quality of their future players is directly linked to the amount of euros they allocate to the development of their grassroots football, although curiously they do not apply this in the budget allocation or policies they follow at youth level.

![Image 93: FC Barcelona](https://soccerinteraction.com/wp-content/plugins/a3-lazy-load/assets/images/lazy_placeholder.gif)

### **International club academies**

Through international academies and campuses around the world, football clubs are looking for financial gain, club growth and branding.

They do not treat internationals the same as their academy academies, as they prioritise the development of those who are “supposedly” most likely to make it as professionals, have been selected by their scouting department and cost them investment.

# Top 4 Football Academies in Spain Which one to choose?

You want to join a football academy, you have read a lot about it, you have asked in forums, in social networks and you are still not sure how to do it and which one to choose to become a professional player.

I hear you. Many of us have gone through this. In this article I will explain what you should take into account before, during and after recruitment.

Below you will find a table with the results of the best academy and we will tell you in detail why. This way you will have everything clearer and you will get it right the first time.

## Comparative guide to the best International Football Academies in Spain

 [raptabla id=’29146′] 
## **Before you decide, you should try a short-term programme.**

Many high performance schools and most professional football academies in general will always give you the option to try before you sign up for an annual programme.

This is because they should be able to assess you, both athletically and psychologically, to ensure that you can successfully complete the programme. As well as clarifying the educational options and homologation of studies.

This programme should include a thorough health check and serve to clarify your goals and how they can help you achieve them, while experiencing part of the programme you will have during the academic year.

## **Under 3 months programme**

Below you will find the offers of the different programmes in order to take into account their differences.

 [raptabla id=’29302′] 
The Short-Term Programme is a course of assessment, personalised coaching and advanced methodology whose main objective is to evaluate both the strengths and weaknesses of a player, as well as the opportunities and threats he will encounter on his path to elite football.

This is the best way to get a taste of what the annual programme is like for the football academy players. It includes everything in the annual programme except the educational offer and options.

The course, which lasts between one and four weeks, can also be used to assess the student’s possible entry into the Professional Programme. In the case of Kaptiva it is only offered for one week. Soccer Inter-Action, however, allows for 1 week to 3 months, making it the most flexible of the three.

## Choosing the right football academy without getting it wrong (detailed guide)

By following this checklist you won’t go wrong and you will be able to really see where the difference is.

### **Aspects to take into account when hiring a football academy**

The following annual programmes of football academies in Spain that we are going to show you on this page meet the following requirements (which would be desirable in a quality professional academy)

### **FACILITIES**

*   Ask if they are owned or rented. If they have all types of surfaces to train on. The availability of natural grass pitches is only available at professional facilities such as the SIA Academy and professional clubs.
*   Is there a beach nearby to practice on sand?

![Image 15: IMG Academy](https://soccerinteraction.com/wp-content/plugins/a3-lazy-load/assets/images/lazy_placeholder.gif)
*   If they are shared or rented, not all training times are available, nor is there a full field all the time where training can be carried out correctly and professionally.

![Image 17: barcelona en sia academy](https://soccerinteraction.com/wp-content/plugins/a3-lazy-load/assets/images/lazy_placeholder.gif)
*   Whether the residence is shared by other guests outside the programme or only for footballers and coaches. In other words, privacy and intimacy.

![Image 19: Fundacion Marcet](https://soccerinteraction.com/wp-content/plugins/a3-lazy-load/assets/images/lazy_placeholder.gif)
*   If the rooms are double or single rooms or shared rooms, is there an extra charge for the double room offer?
*   It has a swimming pool and leisure rooms.

![Image 21: piscina sia academy](https://soccerinteraction.com/wp-content/plugins/a3-lazy-load/assets/images/lazy_placeholder.gif)
*   Do you have gymnasiums and fitness rooms on site?

![Image 23: salas de fitness](https://soccerinteraction.com/wp-content/plugins/a3-lazy-load/assets/images/lazy_placeholder.gif)
*   The age of the installation.

![Image 25: Instalaciones Kaptiva](https://soccerinteraction.com/wp-content/plugins/a3-lazy-load/assets/images/lazy_placeholder.gif)
*   If technology is available. computer rooms, video analysis processing, offices and classrooms for study. Library.

![Image 27: aula video analisis](https://soccerinteraction.com/wp-content/plugins/a3-lazy-load/assets/images/lazy_placeholder.gif)
*   Is the type of menu in the restaurant adapted to players or is it buffet style? Is there a menu for vegans or vegetarians. Halal. Cooking workshop etc. ….

![Image 29: cafeteria soccer inter action](https://soccerinteraction.com/wp-content/plugins/a3-lazy-load/assets/images/lazy_placeholder.gif)
*   If they have a well-equipped clinic or medical service. Physiotherapy room.

![Image 31: clinicanmédica](https://soccerinteraction.com/wp-content/plugins/a3-lazy-load/assets/images/lazy_placeholder.gif)
*   Many academies offer leisure time or close proximity to leisure time or town planning. This is detrimental for an elite athlete who wants to work for a year in a real high performance centre. What they need is privacy and security. Closed and controlled spaces.

![Image 33: foto aerea sia academy](https://soccerinteraction.com/wp-content/plugins/a3-lazy-load/assets/images/lazy_placeholder.gif)
*   Is the city close by and does it have a wide cultural offer?

![Image 35: ciudad de las ciencias](https://soccerinteraction.com/wp-content/plugins/a3-lazy-load/assets/images/lazy_placeholder.gif)
### **SPORTS PROGRAMMING**

Choosing a football boarding school in Spain combines elite training with high-quality education, setting the foundation for success in both sports and academics.

## Why Choose a Football Boarding School in Spain?

As a parent exploring the best opportunities for your child’s football future, you’ll find that Spain stands out as a global leader in football development. The country is an excellent destination for high-quality football training. Choosing a school in Spain can provide your child with several benefits.

### World-Class Training Programs

Spain has cemented its position as a global powerhouse in football, thanks to its prestigious league, La Liga, and consistent success in UEFA competitions. Spanish football is renowned for its technical precision, tactical depth, and fluid style of play, making it an ideal environment for aspiring young athletes. Football boarding schools in Spain incorporate these methods into their training programs, mirroring the high standards of professional clubs. Your child will benefit from advanced coaching methodologies, structured training routines, and exposure to techniques that have shaped some of the greatest players in the world.

### Cultural and Lifestyle Benefits

Beyond football, enrolling in a boarding school in Spain immerses your child in a rich cultural experience. They’ll have the opportunity to learn Spanish, one of the world’s most widely spoken languages, and develop a global perspective by living among diverse peers. The country’s welcoming atmosphere, mild climate, and focus on sports and well-being provide an ideal setting for young athletes to thrive. This well-rounded environment nurtures not just athletic growth but personal development as well.

### Pathways to Professional Opportunities

Football boarding schools in Spain often have direct connections with professional clubs, providing your child with invaluable exposure to proven training methodologies, even scouts and recruitment pathways for the most talented players. These partnerships enhance the chances of advancing to professional academies or even securing trials with top-tier clubs. Many programs proudly showcase alumni who have gone on to sign contracts with professional teams after coming through their Academy, proving the effectiveness of their training methodology and coaching. Choosing a football boarding school in Spain could be the stepping stone your child needs to achieve their potential of playing at the highest level.

## Key Factors When Choosing a Football Boarding School in Spain

### Football Facilities

When evaluating a football boarding school in Spain, the quality of the facilities is very important. Modern pitches, state-of-the-art gym equipment, and access to medical support can significantly impact your child’s development as an athlete. Schools with high-quality training pitches ensure suitable practice environments, while cutting-edge gym facilities allow players to focus on strength and endurance. Additionally, having on-site medical support, such as physiotherapists and sports therapists, ensures that injuries are addressed quickly and effectively, promoting long-term player health.

### Coaching Staff

The expertise and experience of the coaching staff are another important factor in your child’s boarding school experience. Spanish football boarding schools are often staffed with UEFA-certified coaches who bring years of professional and international experience to their programs. These coaches focus on technical skills, tactical understanding, and mental resilience, providing a comprehensive training approach. Researching the backgrounds of coaching staff and their track record with player development is a critical step in the decision-making process.

In football boarding schools in Spain organized by professional Spanish football clubs, the Academy’s actual coaches lead the training sessions to ensure an authentic and high-quality experience for your child. In other boarding school programs in Spain, the program may not be directly connected with a specific club, but UEFA-certified football coaches with many years of experience coaching in high-level academies in Spain deliver the training. Nonetheless, it is important for you to ask the football boarding schools in Spain about the coaching staff that will lead your child’s experience to ensure that it meets your desired level.

### Academics & Well-Rounded Development

Balancing academics and football is essential for young athletes, and top football boarding schools in Spain provide tailored academic programs to support this. Many schools offer flexible schedules, one-on-one tutoring, and accredited curricula, ensuring that students can excel both on the pitch and in the classroom. Emphasis on holistic development—through extracurricular activities, language learning, and cultural engagement—helps students grow into well-rounded individuals prepared for life beyond football.

### Costs & Tuition

Tuition fees for football boarding schools can vary widely, depending on the school’s reputation and the level of facilities offered. In general, costs include training, accommodation, meals, and academic education. Researching available scholarships and budgeting for additional expenses, such as travel or equipment, is a necessary step in the selection process.

### Nationality & Visa Considerations

One factor that is often overlooked but can determine which programs are available to your child is passport and visa eligibility. Some programs, particularly those affiliated directly with La Liga clubs, may have restrictions on how long non-EEA (European Economic Area) players can stay due to Spanish immigration regulations. Others are specifically designed to accommodate international players of all nationalities for a full season, including full visa and residency support. Always clarify eligibility requirements before beginning the application process.

### Atlético de Madrid Football Boarding School

![Image 8: Atletico de Madrid football training complex.](https://oxasport.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/football-training-complex-950x580.jpg.webp)

The Atlético de Madrid Football Boarding School program offers a comprehensive blend of top-tier football training and academic education.

The program includes personalized training sessions with Atlético de Madrid academy coaches, collective training with academy teams, and theoretical seminars to enhance tactical understanding. Athletes can continue their secondary education through partnerships with Vermont Academy and Liceo Europeo, choosing between the International Baccalaureate (IB) or the American Baccalaureate or the traditional Spanish curriculum.

Players also receive a high-performance diet, medical check-ups, and a full range of support services, including accommodation at the official Atlético de Madrid academy residence. Additional benefits include tours of the Metropolitano Stadium and Atlético Territory Museum, internal transfers, and laundry services, ensuring a seamless and enriching experience.

An important consideration for families: participation in the program does not result in an official federation licence for competitive matches, and involvement does not imply any pathway to signing a contract with Club Atlético de Madrid. This is an educational and formative program designed to develop players.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**What is the difference between a football boarding school in Spain and a standard football camp?**
A football boarding school is a full residential program — typically running for a full academic season — where players live, train, study, and develop entirely within the program environment. A football camp runs for days or weeks and focuses purely on intensive training without an academic or long-term residential component. The developmental outcomes are fundamentally different because of the sustained time investment and the consistency of the environment.

**Do all football boarding schools in Spain accept players from outside Europe?**
No, and this is one of the most important distinctions to understand when shortlisting programs. Some programs have full infrastructure to support non-EEA players through visa and residency processes for a complete season. Others have limitations based on Spanish immigration regulations and club structures. Always clarify visa eligibility with Oxasport before applying to any program.

**Are football boarding schools in Spain a guaranteed pathway into a professional club?**
No program can or should promise professional contracts, and any that implies otherwise should be approached with caution. What the best Spanish programs offer is genuine development within elite environments, real visibility in front of professional club staff, and structured pathways for players who demonstrate the required level. These are development programs designed to maximise your child’s potential — not to guarantee a specific outcome.

**Can girls attend football boarding schools in Spain?**
Yes. Several programs on this page — including WOSPAC and the Atlético de Madrid program — explicitly cater to both boys and girls. Contact Oxasport directly for current availability and age-group details for female players across all programs.

**How do I know which Spanish program is the right fit for my child?**
The decision depends on several factors that are specific to your child: their passport and visa situation, current playing level, preferred team structure, academic needs, and whether Madrid, Barcelona, or the Basque Country is the right environment for them. There is no single correct answer that applies to every player. Contact Oxasport for a personalised conversation about your child’s options.

## Why Choose a Football Boarding School in Spain?

As a parent exploring the best opportunities for your child’s football future, you’ll find that Spain stands out as a global leader in football development. The country is an excellent destination for high-quality football training. Choosing a school in Spain can provide your child with several benefits.

### World-Class Training Programs

Spain has cemented its position as a global powerhouse in football, thanks to its prestigious league, La Liga, and consistent success in UEFA competitions. Spanish football is renowned for its technical precision, tactical depth, and fluid style of play, making it an ideal environment for aspiring young athletes. Football boarding schools in Spain incorporate these methods into their training programs, mirroring the high standards of professional clubs. Your child will benefit from advanced coaching methodologies, structured training routines, and exposure to techniques that have shaped some of the greatest players in the world.

### Cultural and Lifestyle Benefits

Beyond football, enrolling in a boarding school in Spain immerses your child in a rich cultural experience. They’ll have the opportunity to learn Spanish, one of the world’s most widely spoken languages, and develop a global perspective by living among diverse peers. The country’s welcoming atmosphere, mild climate, and focus on sports and well-being provide an ideal setting for young athletes to thrive. This well-rounded environment nurtures not just athletic growth but personal development as well.

### Pathways to Professional Opportunities

Football boarding schools in Spain often have direct connections with professional clubs, providing your child with invaluable exposure to proven training methodologies, even scouts and recruitment pathways for the most talented players. These partnerships enhance the chances of advancing to professional academies or even securing trials with top-tier clubs. Many programs proudly showcase alumni who have gone on to sign contracts with professional teams after coming through their Academy, proving the effectiveness of their training methodology and coaching. Choosing a football boarding school in Spain could be the stepping stone your child needs to achieve their potential of playing at the highest level.

## Key Factors When Choosing a Football Boarding School in Spain

### Football Facilities

When evaluating a football boarding school in Spain, the quality of the facilities is very important. Modern pitches, state-of-the-art gym equipment, and access to medical support can significantly impact your child’s development as an athlete. Schools with high-quality training pitches ensure suitable practice environments, while cutting-edge gym facilities allow players to focus on strength and endurance. Additionally, having on-site medical support, such as physiotherapists and sports therapists, ensures that injuries are addressed quickly and effectively, promoting long-term player health.

### Coaching Staff

The expertise and experience of the coaching staff are another important factor in your child’s boarding school experience. Spanish football boarding schools are often staffed with UEFA-certified coaches who bring years of professional and international experience to their programs. These coaches focus on technical skills, tactical understanding, and mental resilience, providing a comprehensive training approach. Researching the backgrounds of coaching staff and their track record with player development is a critical step in the decision-making process.

In football boarding schools in Spain organized by professional Spanish football clubs, the Academy’s actual coaches lead the training sessions to ensure an authentic and high-quality experience for your child. In other boarding school programs in Spain, the program may not be directly connected with a specific club, but UEFA-certified football coaches with many years of experience coaching in high-level academies in Spain deliver the training. Nonetheless, it is important for you to ask the football boarding schools in Spain about the coaching staff that will lead your child’s experience to ensure that it meets your desired level.

### Academics & Well-Rounded Development

Balancing academics and football is essential for young athletes, and top football boarding schools in Spain provide tailored academic programs to support this. Many schools offer flexible schedules, one-on-one tutoring, and accredited curricula, ensuring that students can excel both on the pitch and in the classroom. Emphasis on holistic development—through extracurricular activities, language learning, and cultural engagement—helps students grow into well-rounded individuals prepared for life beyond football.

### Costs & Tuition

Tuition fees for football boarding schools can vary widely, depending on the school’s reputation and the level of facilities offered. In general, costs include training, accommodation, meals, and academic education. Researching available scholarships and budgeting for additional expenses, such as travel or equipment, is a necessary step in the selection process.

### Nationality & Visa Considerations

One factor that is often overlooked but can determine which programs are available to your child is passport and visa eligibility. Some programs, particularly those affiliated directly with La Liga clubs, may have restrictions on how long non-EEA (European Economic Area) players can stay due to Spanish immigration regulations. Others are specifically designed to accommodate international players of all nationalities for a full season, including full visa and residency support. Always clarify eligibility requirements before beginning the application process.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**What is the difference between a football boarding school in Spain and a standard football camp?**
A football boarding school is a full residential program — typically running for a full academic season — where players live, train, study, and develop entirely within the program environment. A football camp runs for days or weeks and focuses purely on intensive training without an academic or long-term residential component. The developmental outcomes are fundamentally different because of the sustained time investment and the consistency of the environment.

**Do all football boarding schools in Spain accept players from outside Europe?**
No, and this is one of the most important distinctions to understand when shortlisting programs. Some programs have full infrastructure to support non-EEA players through visa and residency processes for a complete season. Others have limitations based on Spanish immigration regulations and club structures. Always clarify visa eligibility with Oxasport before applying to any program.

**Are football boarding schools in Spain a guaranteed pathway into a professional club?**
No program can or should promise professional contracts, and any that implies otherwise should be approached with caution. What the best Spanish programs offer is genuine development within elite environments, real visibility in front of professional club staff, and structured pathways for players who demonstrate the required level. These are development programs designed to maximise your child’s potential — not to guarantee a specific outcome.

**Can girls attend football boarding schools in Spain?**
Yes. Several programs on this page — including WOSPAC and the Atlético de Madrid program — explicitly cater to both boys and girls. Contact Oxasport directly for current availability and age-group details for female players across all programs.

**How do I know which Spanish program is the right fit for my child?**
The decision depends on several factors that are specific to your child: their passport and visa situation, current playing level, preferred team structure, academic needs, and whether Madrid, Barcelona, or the Basque Country is the right environment for them. There is no single correct answer that applies to every player. Contact Oxasport for a personalised conversation about your child’s options.

### Personal Statement

I am determined, motivated, and I set high-standard goals for myself. I maintain a 3.55 GPA, while driving myself to be the best soccer player I can be. No matter where I am, on or off the field, I'm willing to improve anything that doesn't live up to my self-expectations. I'm also reminded about my coachable qualities, and am willing to oblige any theme coaches or athletes want to advise me. My determination stands out more than many. For example, I was the first girl from New Hampshire in a long time to be selected for the Eastern States ODP Regional Team with nobody at first to talk to, nor communicate with. I attended the camp determined and I focused on what I was there for. I knew the friends would come later. Within 4 years, I made the US ODP National U17 Squad, proving that overcoming initial step-backs can result in personal success.

I also was invited to spend ten days in a soccer camp held for Malaga FC in Spain called Futbol Carrasco in 2019. Almost nobody there spoke English. This difficulty with communication led to me to initially not understanding the drills or orders from the counselors. On top of that, the girls at hand had a completely alternate team shape and pattern of play. Learning to adapt in situations like this is vital to becoming a leader, and now as High School captain, the lessons I learnt back then will only help me in the future.

Discovering new ways to communicate and comprehend drills in a foreign environment was stressful, but it grew me as a player in a way that not many girls get to experience. Given the opportunity to recognize different styles of play allows me to prove that I will be flexible, and a reliable teammate and student at your college. My leadership, confidence, and determination both on-and off the field divides me from other girls my age; which makes me a perfect fit for your university.

Greta Caulton

April 2022.

### Personal Statement

I am determined, motivated, and I set high-standard goals for myself. I maintain a 3.55 GPA, while driving myself to be the best soccer player I can be. No matter where I am, on or off the field, I'm willing to improve anything that doesn't live up to my self-expectations. I'm also reminded about my coachable qualities, and am willing to oblige any theme coaches or athletes want to advise me. My determination stands out more than many. For example, I was the first girl from New Hampshire in a long time to be selected for the Eastern States ODP Regional Team with nobody at first to talk to, nor communicate with. I attended the camp determined and I focused on what I was there for. I knew the friends would come later. Within 4 years, I made the US ODP National U17 Squad, proving that overcoming initial step-backs can result in personal success.

I also was invited to spend ten days in a soccer camp held for Malaga FC in Spain called Futbol Carrasco in 2019. Almost nobody there spoke English. This difficulty with communication led to me to initially not understanding the drills or orders from the counselors. On top of that, the girls at hand had a completely alternate team shape and pattern of play. Learning to adapt in situations like this is vital to becoming a leader, and now as High School captain, the lessons I learnt back then will only help me in the future.

Discovering new ways to communicate and comprehend drills in a foreign environment was stressful, but it grew me as a player in a way that not many girls get to experience. Given the opportunity to recognize different styles of play allows me to prove that I will be flexible, and a reliable teammate and student at your college. My leadership, confidence, and determination both on-and off the field divides me from other girls my age; which makes me a perfect fit for your university.

Greta Caulton

April 2022.

*   #### Becker Jr., Max '46 - January 22

Max Becker Jr. of Buffalo passed away peacefully on January 22, 2026, at age 97, at home, in the presence of family. He is reunited with the love of his life and wife of 60 years, Cora Hunt Dickinson, who passed in 2010. Max was born in 1928 and attended Nichols School, graduated from Phillips Andover Academy and after graduation from Amherst College in 1950, joined his father at the Buffalo real estate and insurance firm Gurney Becker & Bourne. In October 1950 he married his soulmate, Cora H. Dickinson (Corky). Nine months later, in July 1950, he was activated as part of Headquarters and Headquarters Battery 209 Antiaircraft Artillery Group and served in the Korean War. He and Corky moved to Georgia where Max trained at Camp Gordon, GA; Camp Stewart, GA; and Indiantown Gap Military Reservation. He was deactivated in August 1952 as Master Sargeant. He returned with Corky to Buffalo and resumed his employment with Gurney Becker & Bourne, and his distinguished career in real estate and general insurance. Until November 2025 and for over 70 years prior, he worked at Gurney Becker & Bourne, most recently serving as Chairman. Initially, he worked in residential real estate and insurance. He later changed to include commercial and industrial real estate to his main area of expertise. His clients included General Electric, Chrysler Reality, Nabisco, Kraft, Bayer Supply, Fisher-Price, Jefferson Smurfit, among others. For many years Max was the President of Gurney Becker & Bourne in addition to being active and serving in numerous leadership roles for professional organizations. Most notably, he was a past President of the Society of Industrial and Office Realtors (SIOR) Local Chapter and a National District Vice President and Director. He was a member of the SIOR Legacy Circle. As a result of his long service in the region and volunteer leadership many considered him the dean of commercial real estate in Western New York. He was honored with multiple awards including the New York State Commercial Association of Realtors Lifetime Achievement Award and Buffalo’s Annual Business First Lifetime Achievement “Brick by Brick” Award. Max genuinely cared for Buffalo’s historical significance, responsible future development and economic success. Max also proudly served his beloved community in volunteer leadership roles at multiple Buffalo nonprofits. In 1964, he and Corky were the first husband and wife team to lead the United Way Employee Division. From 1963-1993 he served on the Board of Directors of Millard Fillmore Hospital. Other notable community service roles included: Board of Directors the Blind Association, Vice President Board of Directors Dent Family Foundation, Faculty of the Saturn Club and Vice Dean, Board of Directors Country Club of Buffalo and Secretary. Max and his beloved wife of 60 years, Corky, were proud to be Buffalonians. They were season ticket holders of the Bills and the Sabres and lifetime members of The Saturn Club, the Country Club of Buffalo, the Garrett Club, and Westminster Church where they were married and Max served as a deacon for over a decade. Devoted husband, Max was predeceased by his wife Corky and sisters Joan Becker Crane of Buffalo and Somerset, MA and Francie Becker Braman of Westport, CT. He is survived by his 103 years young sister Barbara Becker Dearborn of Sarasota, FL; children Max Becker, III of Bridgeport, CT and Elizabeth Becker Lenahan of Miami, FL. Four grandchildren also survive him; Lindsey Becker of Maplewood, NJ, Christopher Becker of NYC, Andrew Lenahan of Miami, FL, Kimberly Lenahan of Sao Miguel Island, the Azores, Portugal and 5 Great-Grandchildren: Maggie, Ryan, Avra, Isabel, and Ayla. The family wishes to extend thanks to his doctors, nurses, and caregivers and particularly Team 4 at Hospice for their incredible support and care. Services will be held at Westminster Presbyterian Church February 28, 2026, at 11:00. In lieu of flowers please consider donating in his honor to the Hospice Foundation. Donate online or send a check made payable to: Hospice Foundation, PO Box 590, Buffalo, NY 14240-0590.   
*   #### Berman, Arnold '68 - March 7

Arnold “Arnie” Lewis Berman, a beloved husband, father, grandfather, uncle, attorney, and distinguished athlete, passed away peacefully on March 7. Born on October 2, 1950 in Buffalo, New York, Arnie’s life was defined by excellence — both on the basketball court and in the courtroom.  Arnie grew up with a passion for sports and scholarship, ultimately becoming one of the most iconic figures in Brown University men’s basketball history. Playing from 1969 to 1972, he set multiple scoring and rebounding records and was recognized not only for his athletic prowess but also for his dedication and relentless work ethic. Arnie’s contributions to Brown’s basketball legacy were honored with induction into the Brown University Athletics Hall of Fame (Class of 1978).  After graduating from Brown University, Arnie pursued advanced studies, earning an M.B.A. from New York University and a law degree from the University of Miami School of Law. He dedicated his professional life to practicing law in Florida, ultimately becoming a respected attorney with Shutts & Bowen LLP in West Palm Beach, where he served as a partner and leader in the firm’s litigation group. His legal acumen, integrity, and commitment to his clients made him a trusted name in commercial litigation for decades.  Throughout his legal career, Arnie was known not only as a fierce advocate in the courtroom but also as a mentor and leader among his peers. His contributions helped shape the legal community of South Florida, and his professional legacy will be remembered by those who worked alongside him.  Arnie’s life was deeply enriched by his family. He is survived by his devoted wife, Sondra Berman, his loving daughter Andrea (Kelliher), his son-in-law Christopher Kelliher, and his cherished granddaughter Sloane Kelliher.  A man of boundless energy and curiosity, Arnie balanced his professional commitments with quality time spent with family and friends. He was a mentor, a role model, and a source of enduring love and support to those fortunate enough to know him.  Services to celebrate Arnie’s life will be held at Stanetsky Memorial Chapel in Canton, Massachusetts on March 13 at 1 p.m. In lieu of flowers please consider donating to the American Diabetes Association.

*   #### Burner, Christopher - March 3 (13th Head of School)

Christopher David Burner, 63, of Wilson, New York, died at his home on March 3, 2026. Born on June 16, 1962, in New London, Ohio, he was the son of David L. Burner and Rosemary Hileman Burner. Chris was predeceased by his first wife, Alison Jones Burner. He is survived by his children, Matthew Burner and Abigail Burner; his wife, Amanda Simmons; his parents, David (Sandra) Burner and Rosemary Jones; his sisters, Julia (Stephen) Kalis and Susan (Brandon) Bankowski; and many beloved nieces and nephews.  
Chris grew up in Hudson, Ohio and graduated from Western Reserve Academy in 1980. A natural athlete and leader, he captained both the football and wrestling teams and played defense on the lacrosse team. He continued playing lacrosse at Franklin & Marshall College, where he studied history and political science and earned his B.A. in 1984. During his senior year, trustees at WRA named him the school's College Board Representative.  
Chris began his career in education shortly after college, teaching Latin and coaching wrestling at The St. James School in Hagerstown, Maryland. He soon returned to Western Reserve Academy as a Latin teacher, coach, and Dean of Students, beginning what would become a lifelong commitment to the school and its students.  
While serving at WRA, Chris continued his own academic pursuits. He earned a Master of Liberal Studies from Dartmouth College and, during that same period, took a year away from the Academy to complete a Master of Education at Harvard University in 1990. It was there that he met Alison Jones, who would become his beloved wife of thirty years.  
Chris and Alison were married on December 29, 1990 in Los Angeles, California. The couple moved to Simsbury, Connecticut, where Chris taught and coached at Westminster School before returning to Hudson when he rejoined WRA in 1992 at the encouragement of Dr. Skip Flanagan.  
Back at Western Reserve Academy, Chris served in numerous roles over the years, including Latin teacher, coach of football, lacrosse, and wrestling, Assistant Dean of Administration, Director of Admissions, and Dean of Faculty. Chris and Ali lived on campus for many years in the David Hudson House, where they created a warm and welcoming home at the center of school life.  
During their years in Hudson, Ali built a distinguished career at the Burton D. Morgan Foundation, where for more than two decades she advanced the foundation's mission of supporting entrepreneurship and strengthening communities across Northeast Ohio. Her thoughtful leadership and generosity left a lasting impact on colleagues and the many organizations the foundation supported.  
Their son Matthew was born on July 19, 1993 and their daughter Abigail followed on February 12, 1999. Matt and Abi grew up immersed in both the Hudson community and life at Western Reserve Academy, where they became beloved members of the WRA family.  
The Burner family embraced life in Hudson and often traveled to nearby Cleveland to enjoy its vibrant arts and cultural scene. Summers were frequently spent in Chatham, Massachusetts, where Chris loved boating, fishing, digging for cohogs, and following summer baseball. A self-proclaimed expert at the grill, he delighted in hosting friends and family for long evenings experimenting with new techniques. Through his work in admissions at WRA, Chris also traveled extensively abroad, often bringing Ali, Matthew, and Abigail along on memorable trips to places such as China and Italy.  
Western Reserve Academy appointed Chris as the school's 31st Headmaster in 2008. Over the next decade, he guided the Academy through a period of meaningful growth, leading a record-breaking capital campaign, overseeing campus improvements and restoration projects, and strengthening the school's academic program and student experience.  
In 2019, Chris accepted the position of Head of School at the Nichols School in Buffalo, New York; during this transition, his beloved wife Ali passed away following a courageous battle with glioblastoma.  
Chris assumed the role of 13th Head of School at the Nichols School and quickly became a cherished presence on campus. Known for his thoughtful leadership and approachable style, he believed deeply in the power of community and the importance of listening to the many voices that shape a school. Whether cheering on the hockey team, greeting families at school events, or sharing donuts with his middle school advisees, Chris built genuine connections with students and colleagues alike. In his final year, he found particular joy returning to the classroom to teach Advanced Placement Latin. Many students knew him not only as a teacher and head of school, but as a mentor, advocate, and trusted guide.  
While at Nichols, Chris met Amanda Simmons, whom he married in 2023 in Buffalo, New York. Together they embraced the natural beauty and cultural life of Western New York. Both lovers of classical music, Chris and Amanda frequently attended performances at Kleinhans Music Hall by the Buffalo Philharmonic Orchestra and the Buffalo Chamber Music Society. After their marriage, they settled in Wilson, New York. An avid fisherman, Chris spent many mornings exploring the waters of Lake Ontario, while Amanda devoted time to training their three dogs.  
Chris also contributed widely to the independent school community, serving on the board of Rectory School in Pomfret, Connecticut, participating in NAIS Peer Reviews, and supporting the English-Speaking Union's educational programs.  
While Chris's professional accomplishments were many, those who knew him best remember most his warmth, humor, generosity, and deep devotion to family and friends. He was a proud and loving father, a devoted husband, a cherished son, brother and uncle, and a loyal friend to many. His legacy lives on in the countless students he mentored, the schools he helped shape, and the many communities enriched by his lifelong dedication to education, leadership, and kindness.  
A celebration of Christopher's life will be held at 1 p.m. on Saturday, March 14th, at Trinity Episcopal Church, 371 Delaware Ave., Buffalo, NY. In lieu of flowers, contributions may be made in Chris's name to Nichols School or the Buffalo Philharmonic Orchestra.  
A Memorial Service will be held on Saturday, April 25 at 1:00pm at the Chapel at Western Reserve Academy, 135 College Street, Hudson, Ohio with a reception to follow at Wilson Hall.  
In lieu of flowers, donations may be made in Chris' honor to Western Reserve Academy.  
*   #### Davis, Michael '49 - February 11

A woodsman, an athlete, and most importantly a family man, Michael A. Davis passed away surrounded by family in the Phoenix, Arizona home he loved on February 11th, 2026. A man who liked nothing more than paddling a canoe or sitting with his family watching birds and talking in a stream of consciousness about everything from politics and the state of the world to memorable experiences at Camp Pathfinder (where he took many young campers on their first canoe trips and where there is now a canoe named after him), Nichols School, Cornell University, the U.S. Army as First Lieutenant, Hurwitz Bros. Born in Buffalo at Children's Hospital, young Mickey was an introvert who, with his athletic talents and warm demeanor, found confidence at Nichols School. He went on to study government at Cornell University, where he chose to "perfect his layup" rather than attend his Russian literature class with Vladimir Nabokov; his favorite short story was Hemingway's "The Snows of Kilimanjaro" in part because it illustrated his belief that nature is our greatest solace and teacher.  
  
He could be seen cheering on his favorite baseball team, the St. Louis Cardinals or rooting for his hometown Buffalo Bills, cuddling with his beloved English setters, carefully staking his tomatoes, watching for his resident owl each night, and holding up a finger to shush us all so we could hear the singularly beautiful song of the white-throated sparrow or the strains of Bunny Berigan's "I Can't Get Started" sung by Billie Holiday or Ella Fitzgerald. Hoyt began his career as a reporter for the Niagara Falls Gazette, then worked on WGBH's first local news program before spending two years at Public Broadcast Laboratory, where he produced the environmental documentary "Multiply and Subdue the Earth." He helped create The Advocates in 1969 and served as executive producer of ZOOM in 1974. His body of work includes "LBJ Goes to War," which won an Emmy and a Writers Guild Award, and the acclaimed series Vietnam: A Television History. He earned Peabody Awards for "Crisis in Central America," "Ike"; and 'Reagan," along with a primetime Emmy in 1999 for his biography of Douglas MacArthur. His 2005 program "Victory in the Pacific," a personal favorite, received three Emmy nominations.  
  
Historian David McCullough once counted Hoyt among the finest documentary filmmakers of historical documentaries and biographies of the era, citing his film on Andrew Carnegie, "The Richest Man in the World."  
  
“Austin Hoyt was one of the reasons Boston's PBS station WGBH grew from a regional educational television station in 1969 to the national public television powerhouse it is today,” said Peter McGhee, WGBH’s manager of national programming.  
  
An avid paddler, Hoyt led notable expeditions including a 1959 ascent of the South Nahanni River and a 1962 descent of the Back River to the Arctic Ocean, the first since the nineteenth century. He later authored two books: a 2011 oral history of Bill Levitt and, in 2025, an account of his Nahanni River journey. He was also a devoted sailor and skier, serving for decades on the management committee at Utah's Snowbird resort.  
  
He met Felicity Forbes at the Alta Lodge in 2000 and married her in 2004, building a life together in South Dartmouth.  He was predeceased by his parents, three sisters, and his twin brother. He is survived by his wife, Felicity; her children and grandchildren; several nieces, nephews, and their families; and a stepson.  
  
A life celebration will be held on September 12. Donations in Austin’s memory may be made to The WGBH Educational Foundation or the Dartmouth Natural Resources Trust (DNRT).
